news.title: From Segura to Maltby: six breakout stars from the Women’s Under-20 World Cup
news.lede: With an incredible array of talent on show we select half a dozen players who could make the step up to the senior World Cup next year. The 2026 Under-20 Women’s World Cup is entering the knockout stage in Poland and, after an intriguing group stage, we pick some of the young stars who have stood out. Celia Segura (Spain and Barcelona) Segura is no stranger to knockout football having helped Spain to silver at the Under-17 World Cup two years ago and finishing with the Bronze Ball and Bronze Boot. She has picked up the mantleagain as La Roja eased through their group.

news.title: Scotland call for Sevilla forward Robbie Ure in post-World Cup reset under new coach Pocognoli
news.lede: GLASGOW, Scotland (AP) — A transfer to Spain and change of Scotland coach finally earned Sevilla striker Robbie Ure a first international call Tuesday in a reset after a disappointing World Cup where the Tartan Army of fans far outperformed the team. Scotland’s new coach Sébastien Pocognoli made the 22-year-old Ure the standout inclusion among sweeping changes for four games in a second-tier Nations League group where World Cup quarterfinalist Switzerland starts favorite. news.title: Astana to host 2028 UEFA Super Cup
news.lede: The venue for the 2028 UEFA Super Cup has been confirmed. As reported by İdman.Biz, the UEFA Executive Committee has approved Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan, as the host city for the match. The 2028 UEFA Super Cup will be played at Astana Arena. The traditional season-opening fixture brings together the winners of the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Europa League.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel is still bruised and bitter over England World Cup criticism - does he have a point?
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel still feels very hard done by. In fact, it would be fair to say the England manager has been bruised by the whole World Cup 2026 experience. England finished third in the World Cup, their best-ever performance on foreign soil. So, why are so many England fans still so frustrated, still hurt and why, when looking back upon the summer, do they do it with regret rather than happy memories?

news.title: New Scotland boss calls-up just 14 World Cup players as Oli McBurnie picked for first time in nearly six years
news.lede: The Hull City striker was controversially left out of Steve Clarke's World Cup squad despite helping fire the Tigers to promotion. His omission came despite scoring 17 Championship goals as well as the winner in the play-off final last term. He has since featured in all four of Hull's Premier League outings this season. McBurnie, who has featured 17 times at senior international level, could now win his first cap since appearing against the Faroe Islands in March 2021.

news.title: FIFA President Gianni Infantino Under Scanner After Failed Sell-Off; FIFPRO Demands Change
news.lede: The failed sell-off plan by FIFA boss Gianni Infantino has resulted in FIFPRO, a union for European footballers, to demand changes in the decision structure of the governing body. Infantino had tried to sell stakes in FIFA, and FIFPRO said this exposed how flawed things were. After the FIFA World Cup 2026 final, Infantino proposed to raise $20 billion by selling a 20 percent stake in the body. The backlash resulted in the plan not going through.

news.title: 2030 World Cup: Morocco still insists on the final
news.lede: Spain’s victory in the final of the 2026 World Cup at the expense of Argentina (1-0, ap) officially opened the way for the 24th edition of the World Cup, co-organized by Spain, Morocco and Portugal, with three matches played in Latin America to celebrate the centenary of the competition. While Spain and Morocco are already arguing behind the scenes over the organization of the final, Fouzi Lekjaa, president of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF), continues to demand this final meeting. A few days after affirming that the final of the next World Cup would take place in Casablanca, before being taken over by Fifa, the Moroccan leader was at it again. Also Minister Delegate for the Budget, Fouzi Lekjaa spoke in an interview given to Young AfricaMonday, while he is in the middle of the campaign before the Moroccan legislative elections on September 23.
